title: Can Facing the Truth Improve Outcomes? Effects of Information in Consumer Finance
eligible_reason: Not a staggered DiD. Sections 3-4 (RandomSampleCode_Publication.R) regress checknextmonth (user checks credit score next month) on decreasing_trend = 1(csdiff < 0), a state that switches on and off with each monthly score change, and on left-digit-bias terms (level_change x decreasing_trend) with credit-score level FE, csdiff, account_age and checknum controls, plus user/month/weekday FE in some columns; one column adds a lagged outcome. Tables 7-10 (IV_Publication.do) are an ITT and 2SLS regressions of cs_post_trend on email click_rate with targeting-rule controls, using simulated data. No binary absorbing policy adoption, and every column carries time-varying controls or IV.
design_notes: R (lfe::felm) for descriptive and left-digit regressions; Stata reg/ivregress for Tables 7-10; R simulations for Figure 8. Credit-score monitoring platform data (NDA).

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: time-varying state that switches on/off monthly, time-varying controls, lagged outcome in one column
discontinuity in score level crossing, not policy adoption
IV (email campaigns as instruments) and ITT cross-section; continuous click_rate

data_files_note: README.txt: NDA with data provider, so all data included is simulated (100,000 simulated users; IV data simulated from a covariance matrix).
data_provenance_note: All shipped data simulated per README.txt.
software_notes: R (felm) for Sections 3-4; Stata for IV tables.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text, no PDF). code_prescore 2 from felm with user and month FE; the regressor is a switching credit-score-decline indicator, not a staggered policy.
